questions.stem: Sign: « Le musée est gratuit pour les moins de 26 ans, sur présentation d'une pièce d'identité. » Who gets in free?
options: visitors over 26 who show ID
anyone visiting on the 26th
visitors under 26 who show ID
students of any age with a card
questions.explanation: « Les moins de 26 ans » are people under 26, and « sur présentation d'une pièce d'identité » adds the condition of showing ID. « Moins » means under, not over.

questions.stem: Announcement: « Attention : en raison d'une grève, aucun train ne circulera entre Lyon et Marseille demain. » Why will there be no trains?
options: because of track works
because of an accident
because of a strike
because of bad weather
questions.explanation: « En raison d'une grève » means 'because of a strike'. « Aucun train ne circulera » means that no trains will run at all.

questions.stem: Recipe: « Faites cuire les pâtes dix minutes, égouttez-les, puis ajoutez la sauce. » What do you do straight after cooking the pasta?
options: let it cool
drain it
salt it
rinse it
questions.explanation: « Égoutter » means to drain, and the sauce comes only after that. The text says nothing about salt or cooling.

questions.stem: Email: « Nous regrettons de vous informer que votre commande ne pourra pas être livrée avant le 20 mars. » What is the message?
options: The order has been cancelled
The order was delivered on 20 March
The order will arrive before 20 March
The order will be delayed
questions.explanation: « Ne pourra pas être livrée avant le 20 mars » means it cannot arrive before that date, so it will be late. The order is delayed, not cancelled.

questions.stem: Health campaign slogan: « Mieux vaut prévenir que guérir. » What does it mean?
options: Treatment works better than prevention
It is never too late to get better
Prevention is better than cure
It is better to warn people than to scare them
questions.explanation: « Prévenir » here means to prevent, and « guérir » means to cure. The saying is the exact counterpart of the English proverb.

questions.stem: Advertisement: « Stage d'été : apprenez à surfer en une semaine ! Planches et combinaisons fournies. Places limitées, réservez vite. » What is provided?
options: accommodation for the week
a certificate at the end
boards and wetsuits
transport and meals
questions.explanation: « Fournies » means provided, and « planches » and « combinaisons » are boards and wetsuits. « Un stage » here is a short course, not a work placement.

questions.stem: « Après des années de déclin, la population du village augmente de nouveau grâce à l'arrivée de jeunes familles qui télétravaillent. » What explains the change?
options: a large new factory has opened just outside the village
the village has become a tourist destination
older residents are moving back
young families who work remotely are moving in
questions.explanation: « Grâce à l'arrivée de jeunes familles qui télétravaillent » gives the cause. « De nouveau » shows the population is growing again after its decline.

questions.stem: Interview: « — Qu'est-ce qui vous a poussée à devenir pompière ? — Mon père l'était, et j'ai toujours voulu aider les autres. » What made her choose the job?
options: a love of adventure and danger
a careers program she did in her final year at school
her father's example and a wish to help others
the salary and the job security
questions.explanation: « Mon père l'était » means her father was a firefighter too, and she adds that she always wanted to help others. « Pompière » is the feminine form of « pompier ».

questions.stem: Letter: « Madame, je me permets de vous écrire afin de poser ma candidature au poste de serveur annoncé sur votre site. » What is the purpose of the letter?
options: to complain about poor service
to book a table for a group
to resign from a waiter's job
to apply for a waiter's job
questions.explanation: « Poser sa candidature » means to apply, and « le poste de serveur » is the waiter's position. « Je me permets de » is a polite formal opening.

questions.stem: Forum: « Moi, j'adore l'internat : on est entre copains et on apprend à se débrouiller. Le seul hic, c'est la nourriture ! » What is « le seul hic »?
options: the only reason to stay
the only drawback
the only highlight
the only rule
questions.explanation: « Un hic » is informal for a snag or problem. The writer loves boarding school, so the food is the one thing they dislike.

questions.stem: « J'ai hésité longtemps avant de partir en échange au Québec. Aujourd'hui, je ne regrette rien : j'ai gagné en confiance et en autonomie. » What did the exchange give the writer?
options: better school results
a host family for life
confidence and independence
a job offer from a company in Québec
questions.explanation: « Gagner en confiance et en autonomie » means to grow in confidence and independence. The hesitation was before leaving; the writer now regrets nothing.

questions.stem: « Pour réduire ses déchets, la famille Martin achète en vrac, composte ses épluchures et répare au lieu de jeter. » What does « en vrac » mean here?
options: on special offer
online, for home delivery
in a hurry
loose, without packaging
questions.explanation: « Acheter en vrac » is buying loose goods, often weighed into your own containers, which cuts packaging waste. The context of reducing waste supports this reading.

questions.stem: « Le chef n'utilise que des produits locaux et de saison ; la carte change donc chaque mois. » Why does the menu change?
options: the chef uses only local, seasonal produce
customers ask for new dishes each month
a different chef cooks there each month
the prices of ingredients keep rising
questions.explanation: « Donc » links the monthly menu to the cause just given, « ne… que » meaning 'only'. « La carte » is the menu, not a map.

questions.stem: « Je ne suis pas contre les réseaux sociaux, à condition de savoir s'en déconnecter. » What is the writer's position?
options: The writer cannot stop using social media
It's fine if you know how to switch off
Social media should be avoided altogether
The writer has never used social media
questions.explanation: « Je ne suis pas contre » means 'I'm not against', and « à condition de » sets the condition. The writer accepts social media, with a limit.

questions.stem: « Cher journal, premier jour à Nantes. J'ai le cœur gros : ma famille me manque déjà, mais tout le monde est si gentil ici. » How does the writer feel?
options: overjoyed to be away from home
homesick, though touched by people's kindness
angry that nobody in Nantes has made her welcome
bored with life in Nantes already
questions.explanation: « Avoir le cœur gros » means to feel sad, and « ma famille me manque » means 'I miss my family'. « Mais » adds the comfort of people's kindness.

questions.stem: « Grand-père raconte souvent qu'il allait à l'école à pied, même sous la neige. Nous, on prend le bus, et on se plaint quand même ! » What contrast is drawn?
options: travelling by bus against travelling by car
grandfather's hardship against his grandchildren's complaints
grandfather's comfortable trip against the writer's long walk to school
school in the snow against school in the summer
questions.explanation: The imperfect « allait » describes the grandfather's habit, and « nous… quand même » shows that the writer's generation complains despite an easier life. The tone is self-mocking.

questions.stem: « Bien qu'il ait obtenu son diplôme avec mention, Karim enchaîne les petits boulots depuis un an. » What is Karim's situation?
options: He has a good degree but only casual jobs for a year
He failed his degree and has worked casual jobs since
He is still studying for his degree
He has had a permanent job for a year
questions.explanation: « Bien que » introduces a contrast: a degree with distinction (« avec mention ») yet a string of casual jobs (« enchaîne les petits boulots »). « Depuis un an » means this has gone on for a year.

questions.stem: « Selon le maire, le nouveau centre commercial créera des emplois. Les commerçants du centre-ville craignent, eux, de devoir fermer. » What do the shopkeepers fear?
options: that too few jobs will be created
that the town centre will be rebuilt
that they will have to close down
that the mayor will lose his job
questions.explanation: « Craignent de devoir fermer » means they fear they will have to close. « Eux » sets their view against the mayor's optimism about jobs.

questions.stem: « Les organisateurs se félicitent du succès de la manifestation, qui a réuni deux fois plus de participants que prévu. » What happened?
options: Half as many people came as expected
The organisers apologised for the event
The event was cancelled at short notice
Twice as many people came as expected
questions.explanation: « Deux fois plus… que prévu » means twice as many as planned, and « se féliciter » is to be pleased. « La manifestation » here is an event, not necessarily a protest.

questions.stem: Blog: « Je pensais que vivre à Paris serait un rêve. En réalité, entre le loyer et le bruit, je rêve surtout de vacances ! » What is the tone?
options: wryly humorous
deeply resentful
nostalgic
indifferent
questions.explanation: The writer plays on « rêve », from Paris as a dream to dreaming of a holiday, which makes light of the disappointment. There is complaint, but no real anger.

questions.stem: « Contrairement à ce que l'on croit souvent, les jeunes Français lisent encore beaucoup ; ils lisent simplement autrement, sur écran. » What belief is the writer challenging?
options: that books have become too expensive
that adults read more on screens
that young French people no longer read much
that reading on screen harms young people's concentration
questions.explanation: « Contrairement à ce que l'on croit » introduces a common belief to be corrected, and « lisent encore beaucoup » gives the correction. The writer does not judge screen reading at all.

questions.stem: « Hugo : L'uniforme scolaire efface les différences sociales. — Lina : Il efface surtout notre personnalité ! » How do their views compare?
options: Hugo sees uniforms as equalising; Lina sees them as stifling
Both see uniforms as a way to reduce social differences
Both object to uniforms because they hide personality
Lina agrees with Hugo but adds a condition of her own
questions.explanation: Lina reuses Hugo's verb « efface » to turn his argument around: what uniforms erase, she says, is personality. « Surtout » marks disagreement, not a condition.

questions.stem: « On dit que la cuisine française est compliquée. Pourtant, quoi de plus simple qu'une baguette, un bon fromage et quelques tomates du jardin ? » What is the writer's purpose?
options: to recommend a restaurant in France
to argue that French food can be very simple
to give a recipe for a French meal
to complain about the high price of French food
questions.explanation: « On dit que » introduces a common view and « pourtant » rejects it. The rhetorical question « quoi de plus simple » argues the opposite point.

questions.stem: « Certes, les trottinettes électriques sont pratiques. Encore faudrait-il que leurs utilisateurs respectent les piétons ! » What is the writer's attitude?
options: accepts they are handy but criticises riders' behaviour
rejects electric scooters as useless and dangerous
praises scooter riders for being careful of others
wants pedestrians to give way to scooter riders
questions.explanation: « Certes » concedes the convenience, and « encore faudrait-il que » ('but they would still need to') introduces the criticism. The writer's target is the riders, not the scooters themselves.

questions.stem: « Le lycée a interdit les portables en classe. Les élèves protestent, mais beaucoup reconnaissent, à voix basse, qu'ils se concentrent mieux. » What does « à voix basse » suggest?
options: The students whisper to each other in class
The students are too shy to protest at all
The teachers have asked the students to be quiet
Many admit in private that the ban helps
questions.explanation: « À voix basse » literally means 'in a low voice', but here it suggests a private admission at odds with the public protest. The phrase is figurative, not about whispering in class.

questions.stem: « Je trouvais mes parents trop stricts. Maintenant que je suis moi-même mère, je les comprends mieux… et je les remercie. » How has the writer's view changed?
options: from strict rules as a mother to relaxed ones
from wanting children to deciding against it
from resenting their strictness to gratitude
from admiring her parents to criticising them
questions.explanation: The imperfect « je trouvais » gives the old view; « maintenant que je suis mère » explains the change, and « je les remercie » shows gratitude. Becoming a parent changed her perspective.

questions.stem: « Ce n'est pas parce qu'on est jeune qu'on n'a rien à dire sur l'avenir de la planète. » What is the writer arguing?
options: Young people have nothing useful to say about the planet's future
The planet's future depends only on the decisions of young people
Only older people should decide about the future of the planet
Being young does not mean having nothing to say on the planet's future
questions.explanation: « Ce n'est pas parce que… que » rejects a supposed cause-and-effect link: youth does not mean having nothing to say. Missing the first negative turns the sentence into its opposite.

questions.stem: « Il aurait suffi d'un peu de bon sens pour éviter cette catastrophe. » What does the writer imply?
options: The disaster could not have been avoided
Common sense was the cause of the disaster
The disaster is likely to happen again
The disaster could easily have been avoided
questions.explanation: « Il aurait suffi de » ('all it would have taken was') points to something simple that was not done. The conditional perfect describes what could have happened but did not.

questions.stem: « Ils ont entre 15 et 18 ans, viennent des quatre coins de la France et partagent une même passion : la robotique. » What is this most likely to be?
options: a step in an instruction manual
an entry in a personal diary
the opening of a magazine feature article
the opening of a formal letter of complaint
questions.explanation: Introducing a group in the third person to draw readers in is typical of a feature article's opening. A formal letter would begin with an address such as « Madame, Monsieur ».

questions.stem: « “Le Petit Prince” a été traduit en des centaines de langues. Sa phrase la plus célèbre, “On ne voit bien qu'avec le cœur”, reste d'actualité. » What does « reste d'actualité » mean?
options: remains relevant today
has been in the news lately
is now out of date
has never been translated
questions.explanation: « Rester d'actualité » means to remain topical or relevant. « Actuel » and « actualité » are false friends: they refer to the present, not to what is 'actual'.

questions.stem: « Ma correspondante m'a appris une expression québécoise : “c'est plate”, qui veut dire “c'est ennuyeux”. » In Québec, what does « c'est plate » mean?
options: it's cheap
it's easy
it's boring
it's flat
questions.explanation: The text defines it: « qui veut dire “c'est ennuyeux” ». Reading « plate » literally as 'flat' ignores the definition given in the text itself.

questions.stem: « La Martinique attire chaque année de nombreux touristes, mais ses habitants s'inquiètent de la hausse du coût de la vie. » What worries the residents?
options: pollution of the beaches
the lack of jobs on the island
the rising cost of living
the number of tourists
questions.explanation: « S'inquiéter de » means to worry about, and « la hausse du coût de la vie » is the rising cost of living. The tourists are mentioned, but « mais » moves to the real concern.

questions.stem: Notice at a sports centre: « Objets trouvés : les objets non réclamés au bout de trois mois seront donnés à une association. » What happens to unclaimed items?
options: They are given to a charity after three months
They are thrown away after three months
They are sold at the centre every three months
They are kept for three months, then posted back
questions.explanation: « Non réclamés » means unclaimed, « au bout de trois mois » means after three months, and « donnés à une association » means given to a charity or community group.

questions.stem: Sign at a bike path: « Le port du casque est obligatoire pour les cyclistes de moins de douze ans. » Who must wear a helmet?
options: all cyclists of any age
cyclists over twelve
parents riding with children
cyclists under twelve
questions.explanation: « Le port du casque » is the wearing of a helmet, and « de moins de douze ans » limits the rule to children under twelve. « Le port » here has nothing to do with a harbour.

questions.stem: Text message: « Je serai en retard ce soir, réunion imprévue. Mange sans moi, bisous. Maman » What does the mother say?
options: She has forgotten a meeting and is very sorry
She has an unexpected meeting, so eat without her
She has planned a meeting and will cook later
She is on her way home, so wait for her to eat
questions.explanation: « Imprévue » means unforeseen, and « mange sans moi » tells her child to eat without her. Nothing suggests she wants anyone to wait.

questions.stem: Shop window: « Soldes : jusqu'à moins cinquante pour cent sur toute la collection d'hiver ! » What is on offer?
options: half off a few items from the winter range
a fixed fifty euros off any winter item
up to half off the whole winter collection
fifty new items in the winter collection
questions.explanation: « Les soldes » are sales, and « jusqu'à moins cinquante pour cent » means reductions of up to 50 per cent. « Toute la collection » covers the whole range, not a few items.

questions.stem: Sign in a town hall: « Pour tout renseignement, adressez-vous à l'accueil, au rez-de-chaussée. » Where do you go for information?
options: to the mayor's office upstairs
to reception on the ground floor
to the office on the first floor
to the information website
questions.explanation: « L'accueil » is reception, and « le rez-de-chaussée » is the ground floor. In France « le premier étage » is the floor above it.

questions.stem: Review: « On attendait beaucoup de ce deuxième roman. Hélas, l'intrigue s'essouffle dès la moitié du livre. » What is the reviewer's verdict?
options: The novel matches the success of the first one
The plot moves too quickly to follow
The novel disappoints as its plot runs out of steam
The second half is better than the first
questions.explanation: « On attendait beaucoup » sets up high expectations, « hélas » signals disappointment, and « s'essouffler » (to run out of breath) means the plot loses momentum halfway.

questions.stem: « Le gouvernement assure que la réforme sera “indolore” pour les ménages. Les syndicats, eux, appellent déjà à la grève. » What does the second sentence suggest?
options: The government has already called a strike against the reform
The reform has been cancelled because of strike action
The unions doubt the reform will be as painless as claimed
The unions agree that households will not be affected
questions.explanation: The quotation marks around « indolore » distance the writer from the government's word, and « eux » with « déjà » shows the unions reacting against it straight away. Calling a strike implies they expect the reform to hurt.

questions.stem: « Ce petit village breton, longtemps oublié des touristes, est devenu en quelques années une destination à la mode. » What has changed?
options: A village has always been a fashionable destination
Tourists have stopped visiting Brittany entirely
A village long ignored by tourists has become fashionable
A popular village has been forgotten by tourists
questions.explanation: « Longtemps oublié » describes the past, and « est devenu en quelques années » the recent change. « À la mode » means fashionable.
